setup: Lean your back and hips on a wall
Feet out in front, legs straight
execution: Pull your toes up toward your shins
Lift them as high as you can
Lower slowly until they almost touch
Keep your heels on the floor
faults: Don't bounce your toes off the floor
Don't bend your knees to help

notes: Feet further from the wall make it harder; start close and move out.
The front of the shin tires quickly and can burn. Stop the set when the range gets short.
This is a training exercise for the front of the shin. It makes no claim about preventing or treating shin pain.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Seated toe raises
regressions.reason: Sitting on a bench with feet flat; lighter and easier to control.

progressions.name: Feet further from the wall
progressions.reason: More body lean puts more weight through the shins.

progressions.name: Tib bar raise
progressions.reason: Seated on a high bench with plates on a tib bar; loadable. Logs a weight, so it would be its own entry.

substitutions.name: Band toe pull
substitutions.reason: Seated with a band around the top of the foot, anchored in front.

substitutions.name: Heel walks
substitutions.reason: Walking on the heels with toes up works the same muscle with no kit.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at shin height, figure facing right with the wall behind. Shows the lean on the wall and the toes lifting while the heels stay down.

keyPositions.label: Down
keyPositions.describe: Back and hips resting on the wall, legs straight, feet about a foot-length or two from the wall. Heels and toes on the floor.

keyPositions.label: Up
keyPositions.describe: Toes lifted as high as possible toward the shins, heels still on the floor. Body still leaning on the wall.
